justification: Loaded-framing upgrade prompt: social proof (2,000,000+ on pro), 'deal of the year', 'last chance', 'promo price valid today only' — fabricated urgency and pressure to upgrade.
Purchase flow with countdown, but fully transparent: terms visible (auto-renew $49/mo, cancel anytime, no refunds), timer labelled 'nothing auto-confirms' and 'take the time you need'.
False exclusivity ('You've been selected for an exclusive offer', 'valued customer') pushing a free-trial that auto-renews at $49.99/mo full price — manipulative trial framing despite the disclosure.
Account deletion flow: one-click delete, request confirmed, 30-day deletion window and progress bar shown transparently; no obstruction.
Insurance comparison: 8 policies with upfront monthly prices and expandable 'Policy details (fine print)' (excess, breakdown, courtesy car); honest comparison.
Account creation: ToS/data-sharing checkbox starts unchecked and explicitly notes acceptance only on active tick — honest opt-in.
Contacts permission prompt discloses purpose (match contacts to find friends) and is labelled read-only; grant flow straightforward.
Locked-episode rental paywall: $3.99 one-time price stated clearly, dismissible 'Later' button, plays after rent — no manipulation.
One-time Pro license $79, 'no subscription, no renewal', amount on button; instant charge without review step is disclosed in text.
Camera app: location-tags toggle off by default, explicitly 'Optional — the camera works either way'. Privacy-respecting.

Sneaked add-on: cart shows 2 items (headphones + $19.99 Extended Warranty) though user added 1; total includes the unrequested warranty and a 'quick check' tricks the user into confirming the wrong count.
Fake competition: 'You vs Al/Alex' battle where the scripted opponent sits at a fixed 70 while your score climbs; 'loser gets demoted a league' loss-aversion pressure to keep answering.
Privacy settings: ad-data sharing off by default, data minimization on by default, both options equal visual weight — honest defaults.
Product page: 4.1 stars from 1,284 real reviews, explicitly 'including the negative ones', link to read all reviews — honest ratings.
Dual-price anchoring: strikethrough PLN 299 reference with no factual baseline shown ('Why the slash?' admits no baseline), 'you save 33%' and 'while stocks last' scarcity.
Seasonal event with countdown, but explicitly framed as a fact ('timer is just a fact — play whenever you like'); transparent, no fake urgency.
No cancel affordance: auto-renewing premium after trial with no cancellation button anywhere; only 'Proceed with renewal' — forced continuation.
Checkout nudges account creation with perks framing, but a clear 'Continue without benefits' guest option exists; persuasive but not deceptive.

HighDemand#3: '2,000,000+ users on pro' numeric quantifier with no temporal/geographic qualifier (unfalsifiable); FOMO#3: high urgency-lexeme density ('last chance', 'valid today only', 'deal of the year'); PersuasiveLanguage coercion density. Badge itself reads 'Loaded framing'.

CountdownTimer#3 negative: no amplifying lexemes — text explicitly says 'nothing auto-confirms' and 'take the time you need'; HiddenInformation negative: auto-renew ($49/mo) and cancel policy listed verbatim in terms; confirmation language present ('I have read the terms — confirm purchase').

ForcedContinuity#1: 30-day $0 trial auto-converts to $49.99/mo without explicit consent at conversion; PrivacyZuckering#1: marketing-consent checkbox gates the (disabled-until-checked) activation button, bundling monetization consent with service activation; 'selected for an exclusive offer' is unfalsifiable loaded framing.

ForcedGracePeriod#1: T_execute - T_request = 720h (30 days) >> threshold 24h, a programmatic constraint; #2: no cancellation affordance rendered during the waiting window (progress bar only, no reversal vector in states s1-s3). Transparency of the progress display does not negate the delay condition.

No ontology condition fires: prices shown upfront, fine print (excess, breakdown, courtesy car) disclosed in expandable details elements; 'Most popular' badge alone does not meet FalseHierarchy/AsymmetricDominance thresholds (no decoy, no structural downgrade).

BadDefaults#1 negative: State(c,t0)=False (unchecked); AutomaticAccept#3 negative: box not pre-checked, no auto-consent; TrickQuestions#3 negative: zero negations in label; explicit note 'acceptance happens only when you actively tick this box'.

FriendSpam#1 negative: prompt is read-only matching ('matches your contacts... find friends'), no SendMessages path; AddressBookLeeching#1 negative: permission serves the stated core function (contact matching), no utility-permission decoupling; Granting&Interaction#3 negative: no scope creep.

PayToPlay#2 negative: unlock prompt is a compact inline bar, dismissible via 44px-min 'Later' button; #3 negative: framed as transaction ('Rent $3.99' one-time), not as 'unlock'; no artificial free-path friction (locked content is the rental model, not exponential grinding).

ReducedFriction#1: financial-domain one-click purchase bypasses confirmation interstitial (E_click(intent)->commit, S_confirm not in path — page states 'No review step — your card is charged instantly'); #3: no confirmation-seeking language ('Are you sure?') precedes the $79 charge. Disclosure does not restore the removed decision boundary.

BadDefaults#1 negative: location-tags toggle off at t0 ('Tags: off'); semantic intent check negative — off-by-default is privacy-preserving, not provider-favorable; Granting&Interaction negative: camera permission is the app's core function.

SneakIntoBasket#1: I_cart \ I_explicit = {2-Year Extended Warranty $19.99} — cart shows 2 items though only 1 was added, total $149.98 includes the unrequested item; #2: warranty row rendered visually identical to user items; Bundling#1: no discrete event to add headphones alone; 'quick check' prompts user to (wrongly) confirm '1 item'.

EncouragingAntiSocialBehavior#2: binary competitive split layout (You vs Alex scoreboards, ratio ~0.5) with loss-aversion framing 'loser gets demoted a league'; opponent score static at 70 while user climbs 0->34 — scripted, unfalsifiable competition pressuring continued answering.

BadDefaults#1 negative: ad-data sharing off at t0 (aria-checked=false), data-minimization on (user-favorable default, intent not in provider domains); PrivacyZuckering#2 negative: equal visual weight stated and rendered; ChoiceOverload negative: 2 toggles only.

Endorsement&Testimonials#1 negative: mean 4.1 with organic variance (not ~5.0, Var~0); #3 negative: no templated/stock endorsements; HighDemand#3 negative: 1,284-review count is a review tally, not an unbounded demand quantifier; negative reviews explicitly included.

ReferencePricing#3: P_ref (PLN 299) > P_cur (199) with line-through CSS — anchoring active; interface's own 'Why the slash?' text confirms 'no factual baseline is shown'; #2: ref rendered small/muted vs dominant current price; LimitedTimeMessage/FOMO: 'while stocks last' scarcity lexeme.

CountdownTimer#3 negative: adjacent text neutralizes urgency ('The timer is just a fact — play whenever you like'); LowStock#3 negative: '3 rewards left' stable across s1/s2 (no procedural inconsistency); LimitedTime#1 negative: no extension; specific deadline visible (no ambiguous bounding).

ImmortalAccounts#3: K_del (delete/cancel) ∩ T_DOM = ∅ — no termination vector exists (badge 'No cancel button', note 'cancel not in the dom'); ForcedContinuity#1: trial already converted to auto-renewing €9.99/mo with no explicit consent at conversion; only action offered is 'Proceed with renewal'.

ForcedRegistration#2: guest pathway is a small text-only link vs full-width high-contrast 'Create account & check out' button (visual-weight ratio below guest-visibility threshold); #3: guest label loss-framed — 'Skip for now — you'll miss out on member perks, faster delivery, and exclusive deals' (negative sentiment). #1 negative (guest path exists), but #2+#3 trigger the pattern.
